questions.q: What does the summary call the core of capitalism?
a: Using money or capital to make more money
Saving as much income as possible
Sharing profits equally among workers
Letting governments direct investment
questions.why: Lesson 1 says capitalists put capital to work to earn a return, with profit being what is left after costs.

questions.q: How can a home serve as capital for an individual?
a: Sell it for its equity or rent it for income
Live in it without paying any rent
Borrow against it to fund vacations
Pass it down as a tax-free inheritance
questions.why: Lesson 1 gives the home as an example of an asset that can be sold for equity or rented for monthly revenue.

questions.q: Why did capitalism's roots take hold in medieval Europe?
a: Power was split among many competing states
A single emperor controlled all trade
The church banned lending and markets
Guilds owned most of the farmland
questions.why: Lesson 2 points to a fragmented political system with multiple jurisdictions, unlike Rome or China's dynasties.

questions.q: What did low interest rates after 2008 lead to in developing nations?
a: More borrowing, setting up a future crash
Rapid repayment of their debts
An end to trade with the West
Nationalization of their banks
questions.why: Lesson 3 says cheap credit eased pressure in the West but encouraged developing countries to borrow heavily.

questions.q: Why is it hard to fix the crises built into capitalism?
a: Big corporations resist rules that limit short-term profit
Economists still disagree on what caused 2008
Banks have already moved to stricter countries
Voters reject every kind of regulation
questions.why: Lesson 3 notes that powerful corporations favor short-term gains and push back against tougher oversight.
